footnotes: Notes. (1) Aigun was in 1922 made a customs station independent of Harbin. (10) By an Agreement dated May 30, 1907, Japan undertook to place the Dairen Customs under the control of the Maritime Customs. (15) Hunchun, Kirin province, was made a sub-port of Lungchingtsun in July 1924. (17) By an Agreement dated Dec. 2 1905, Germany placed the Kiaochao Customs under the control of the Maritime Customs, though the European staff of the Customs was to be of German nationality. A similar agreement was signed on Aug. 6, 1915, by which Japanese were to be appointed to the posts previously held by Germans, and the Customs duties, less 20% were to be turned over to the Chinese Maritime Customs. This arrangement has now been cancelled by the Shantung Settlement. (25) Lungkow is in the Chefoo customs district. (26, 34, and 39) Manchouli, Sansing and Suifenho have been made part of the Harbin customs district. (42) Tatungkow is in the Antung customs district. (48) The Customs station at Yatung, Tibet, was closed in 1912. Establishment of a customs station at Weihaiwei is under advisement. It has been delayed until the details connected with handing this territory back to Chinese administration are settled
